Fact.Name: Part of the QEF distribution above line 8a shown to have been included in income before
Fact.Description: Screen specification. QUESTION: "Your distributions from this QEF on line 8b are more than the amount you include in income for the year on line 8a. How much of that excess can you show, with the statement the instructions describe, was already included in your income, or in the income of another U.S. person, in an earlier year?" HELP TEXT: "The excess is treated as paid out of the QEF's most recently accumulated earnings and profits. It is not taxable to the extent you can show it was previously included in your income or another U.S. person's income; attach the statement listed under Attachments for Election E (the person's name, address and identifying number, the amount and year included, the provision of law, and how you acquired the stock). Any part you cannot show is taxed under section 301(c) as a dividend." (Instructions for Form 8621, Line 8.) ASKED WHEN: the fund is a QEF (../isQef is Yes) and line 8b is more than line 8a. UNANSWERED: REFUSED: the fund's dividend and the return's Form 8621 dividends stay unresolved; defaulting either way misstates income. VALIDATION: a dollar amount, zero or more; an amount above the excess is read as the whole excess. FEEDS: ../qefDistributionDividend.

Fact.Name: QEF distributions above the year's inclusion (line 8b over line 8a)
Fact.Description: For a QEF, the amount by which the line 8b distributions exceed the line 8a inclusion, never below zero; $0 when the fund is not a QEF or line 8b is unanswered. The instructions treat this excess as paid out of the QEF's most recently accumulated earnings and profits.

Fact.Name: QEF distribution taxed under section 301(c) as a dividend
Fact.Description: The part of ../qefDistributionExcess the filer does not show was previously included in income (../writableLine8bExcessPreviouslyIncluded), taxed under section 301(c). Treated wholly as a dividend: the instructions treat the excess as paid out of the most recently accumulated earnings and profits (TAX-INTERPRETATIONS IN-50). Never a qualified dividend, because a dividend from a passive foreign investment company is excluded from qualified dividend income. $0 when there is no excess; when there is one and the previously-included question is unanswered this is Incomplete.

Fact.Name: Total tax figured without the undistributed earnings of every fund making election B
Fact.Description: Screen specification. QUESTION: "You are making election B for more than one fund. What would your total tax for 2025 be if your taxable income did not include the undistributed earnings (line 8e) of ANY of those funds?" HELP TEXT: "Figure your total tax the same way as for line 9b, but leave out the line 8e amounts of all the funds for which you make election B at the same time. The tax whose payment you may extend is your total tax minus this amount (section 1294(b)); adding each fund's own line 9c can extend more than that when the funds push your income into higher brackets." ASKED WHEN: two or more funds on the return have a line 9c amount above zero (election B made and permitted). UNANSWERED: REFUSED: the return's deferred tax (/form8621CurrentTaxDeferral) and Form 1040 line 24 stay unresolved. VALIDATION: a dollar amount, zero or more, not more than the line 9a total tax. FEEDS: /form8621CurrentTaxDeferral. Like line 9b it is a retained counterfactual computation the filer supplies: the graph computes one return, not a second one without these inclusions.

Fact.Name: PFIC stock value counted for the $25,000 Part I exception
Fact.Description: The Part I line 4 values of every fund on the return, leaving out stock owned through another U.S. person or another PFIC: the total the $25,000 ($50,000 joint) exception to Part I tests on the last day of the tax year. It assumes the fund list holds every PFIC the filer owns. Incomplete while the fund list or a counted value is.

Fact.Name: Total Form 8621 CurrentTaxDeferral
Fact.Description: Every Form 8621 Part III line 9c on this return added together and capped at line 9a; with two or more deferring funds also capped at line 9a less /writableForm8621TotalTaxWithoutElectedUndistributedEarnings, the tax figured without all of their undistributed earnings, which is the section 1294(b)(1) excess measured once for the return (TAX-INTERPRETATIONS IN-51). Form 1040 line 24 is the total tax before this deferral less this amount, so the cap is what keeps line 24 from going below zero: each fund's line 9a is the WHOLE return's tax, not that fund's share of it, so two or more funds electing to defer under section 1294 produce line 9c amounts that overlap, and their untrimmed sum exceeds the tax being deferred. The instructions license subtracting the deferred tax from the sum of lines 22 and 23; they do not license a negative total tax. The cap is a floor on the return, not an allocation: the multiple-election allocation of Temp. Reg. 1.1294-1T is NOT modelled here, so a return with two or more elected QEFs gets the right total (the whole tax deferred, nothing more) and the wrong split between the funds. Resolves $0 when the collection is empty or absent.

Fact.Name: This PFIC's stock is owned through another U.S. person or through another PFIC
Fact.Description: Screen specification. QUESTION: "Do you own this PFIC's stock through another U.S. person (for example a U.S. partnership or trust) or through another PFIC?" HELP TEXT: "Stock you own that way does not count toward the $25,000 ($50,000 on a joint return) total that can excuse you from Part I." (Instructions for Form 8621, Exceptions To Filing Part I.) ASKED WHEN: for every fund. UNANSWERED: the fund is counted toward the total; if that decides the exception, Part I is treated as required (the conservative print). VALIDATION: Yes or No. FEEDS: ../valueCountedForPartIThreshold.

Fact.Name: This PFIC's stock is owned indirectly
Fact.Description: Screen specification. QUESTION: "Do you own this PFIC's stock indirectly, through a foreign entity, rather than directly?" HELP TEXT: "If you own it indirectly and your proportionate share is worth $5,000 or less on the last day of your tax year (Part I line 4), you may not need to complete Part I for it, unless you received an excess distribution or had a gain on a disposition." (Instructions for Form 8621, Exceptions To Filing Part I.) ASKED WHEN: for every fund. UNANSWERED: treated as direct ownership for the exception; Part I then prints unless another exception applies. VALIDATION: Yes or No. FEEDS: ../partIRequired.

Fact.Name: The fund is a section 1291 fund (neither a QEF nor marked to market)
Fact.Description: True when the fund is neither treated as a QEF (../isQef) nor under the section 1296 mark-to-market election (../markToMarket); Incomplete while either is unanswered.

Fact.Name: The fund produced an excess distribution or a disposition gain this year
Fact.Description: True when any Part V transaction of the fund has an excess distribution or disposition gain to allocate (../section1291Transactions/*/excessToAllocate above zero).

Fact.Name: Part I line 4 value counted toward the $25,000 Part I threshold
Fact.Description: The fund's Part I line 4 value, unless the filer owns it through another U.S. person or another PFIC (then $0). An unanswered ownership question counts the value. A value entered below $0 counts as $0 (the line 4 bands start at $0).

Fact.Name: Form 8621 Part I is required for this fund
Fact.Description: False only when one of the two value exceptions to Part I applies: the fund is a section 1291 fund that produced no excess distribution or disposition gain this year, and either the filer's PFIC stock counted for the threshold (/form8621PartIAggregateValue) is $25,000 or less ($50,000 or less on a joint return), or the filer owns this fund indirectly and its Part I line 4 value is $5,000 or less. True otherwise, including when an answer the exceptions need is missing: the conservative print. The estate, trust and chain-of-ownership exceptions of the instructions are not modelled. Read by the application to decide whether Part I prints; no tax amount depends on it.
